issues.reason: The genitive rule explicitly carves a nominalization's argument out of Possession (the of-object exclusion) and states nothing for a nominalization's possessive SUBJECT, while the temporal-anchor rule's 'nothing else' is glossed as 'no tense or status of its own, because the clause predicates nothing of it' — so with an event-noun treated as an eventuality (the light-verb rule), (Agent sk_retirement_1 foley) is true of 'his retirement', well-typed, and acceptable improvisation in gap territory.

Compound concepts makes modifier exposure determined by the predication test — '*the secretary is assistant' fails, and a non-predicable modifier is 'never exposed' — so (Inheritance assistant_secretary_of_energy_for_defense_programs assistant) is an unlicensed atom that also mis-states a rank title as membership in the kind 'assistant'.

Names and casing requires the entity's kind in one ordinary type atom 'whether the kind word sits inside the name or beside it' (the Kestrel River / Brindle estuary precedent), so (Member ronald_reagan president) is traceable to the words, true and well-typed; the Dr-Okoro clause bars inferring a relation (kinship) from a title, not a kind atom.

gaps_confirmed: a multi-word office title carrying of/for PP arguments ('assistant secretary of energy for defense programs') — Compound concepts licenses only modifier_noun fusion, and nothing says how the complements attach
the possessive subject of an event nominalization ('his retirement') — only the of-phrase object and the plain genitive are covered
an occupational/office title before a name ('President Ronald Reagan') — the title rule fixes the Name string but does not say whether a companion kind atom is also licensed
new_gaps: a rank/attributive-only modifier ('assistant secretary', 'deputy chief') — the predication test bars exposing it, so once fused the rank is recorded nowhere; no licensed atom carries it
repair_summary: Removed (Inheritance assistant_secretary_of_energy_for_defense_programs assistant); the head-noun genus and every other atom are unchanged.
notes: As and Under are preposition-named obliques on the event and are licensed, and the after-clause correctly yields Before with no connective atom and no tense on the anchor.
